<!-- note-1: body_md -->
\label{n:1}
Let us formulate known results on this topic.

\smallskip
(i)
$K$-Analytic (in particular, Souslin) spaces are universally $\sigma$-measurable \cite[7.14.125]{Bogachev2007Measure_theory}.

\smallskip
(ii)
A space $X$ is universally $\tau$-measurable if and only if $X$ is $\mu$-measurable in $\beta X$ for any measure $\mu\in P(\beta X)$ \cite[Example 7.14.22]{Bogachev2007Measure_theory}.

\smallskip
(iii)
A paracompact space $X$ is universally $[\sigma,\tau]$-measurable if and only if $X$ does not contain an Ulam-measurable discrete closed subset
(see~\cite[Theorem I.28]{Varadarajan1965measures} and \cite[Section 2]{BanakhChigogidzeFedorchuk2003}). In particular, a Lindelöf space is a universally $[\sigma,\tau]$-measurable space \cite[Corollary 2.2]{BanakhChigogidzeFedorchuk2003}.

\smallskip
(iv)
For a space $X$, the following conditions are equivalent \cite[Theorem 1.22]{Reznichenko2025betap}:
(a) $X$ is pseudocompact;

(b) $X$ is a universally $[\sigma,a]$-measurable space.
<!-- end note-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{t:gum:1}
For a space $X$, the following statements are equivalent:
\begin{itemize}
\item[{\rm (i)}]
$X$ is universally $\tau$-measurable;
\item[{\rm (ii)}]
$X$ is $\mu$-measurable in $\beta X$ for any measure $\mu\in P(\beta X)$;
\item[{\rm (iii)}]
there exists an embedding of space $X$ into some space $Y$ such that
$X$ is $\mu$-measurable in $Y$ for any measure $\mu\in P(\beta Y)$;
\item[{\rm (iv)}]
for any embedding of space $X$ into any space $Y$,
$X$ is $\mu$-measurable in $Y$ for any measure $\mu\in P(\beta Y)$.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{p:umnR}
A space $X$ is universally $R$-measure zero if and only if every compact subset of $X$ is scattered.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{p:umnR-ast}
Let $p\in\{a,\sigma,\tau\}$.
A space $X$ is universally of $p$-measure zero if and only if $X$ is universally $p$-measurable and
every compact subset of $X$ is scattered.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- problem-1: body_md -->
For $p,q\in\{f,\sigma,\tau,R,\beta,d\}$ and $Q\in \{M,M^+,U,U^+,P\}$, describe universally
${[a,b]}$-measurable, universally $Q_{[a,b]}$-measurable, and universally $Q^\ast_{[a,b]}$-measurable spaces.
<!-- end problem-1 -->
<!-- note-2: body_md -->
Let us formulate known results on this topic.

\smallskip
(i)
If $X$ is a universally $\sigma$-measurable space and the finite powers $X^n$ of $X$ have a countable Souslin number (in particular, $X$ is a Souslin space), then $X^\kappa$ is a universally $P_\sigma$-measurable space for any cardinal $\kappa$ \cite[Corollary 5.2]{BanakhChigogidzeFedorchuk2003}.

\smallskip
(ii)
Any $AE(0)$-space is a universally $P_\sigma$-measurable space \cite[Corollary 5.3]{BanakhChigogidzeFedorchuk2003}.

\smallskip
(iii)
For a space $X$, the following conditions are equivalent \cite[Theorem 1.22]{Reznichenko2025betap}:
(a) $X$ is pseudocompact;
(b) $X$ is a universally $[\sigma,a]$-measurable space;
(c) $X$ is a universally $P_{[\sigma,a]}^\ast$-measurable space.

\smallskip
(iv)
For a space $X$, the following conditions are equivalent \cite[Theorem 1.27]{Reznichenko2025betap}:
(a) $X$ is pseudo $\omega$-bounded;
(b) $X$ is a universally $P_{[\beta,a]}^\ast$-measurable space.

\smallskip
(v)
For a space $X$, the following conditions are equivalent \cite[Theorem 1.9]{Reznichenko2025betap}:
(a) $P(X)$ is pseudocompact;
(b) $X$ is a universally $P_{a}^\ast$-measurable space.

\smallskip
(vi)
For a space $X$ with precaliber $\omega_1$, the following conditions are equivalent \cite[Theorem 1.28]{Reznichenko2025betap}:
(a) $P_\tau(X)$ is pseudocompact;
(b) $X$ is a universally $P_{[\tau,a]}^\ast$-measurable space.
<!-- end note-2 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{t:main:1}
Let $X$ be a space and $p,q\in\{a,\sigma,\tau,R,\beta,d\}$. The following conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[{\rm (i)}]
$X$ is a universally $M_{[p,q]}$-measurable space;
\item[{\rm (ii)}]
$X$ is a universally $M^\ast_{[p,q]}$-measurable space;
\item[{\rm (iii)}]
$M_p(X)$ is $G_\delta$-dense in $M_{q}(X)$;
\item[{\rm (iv)}]
For a measure $\mu \in M_q(X)$ and a sequence of functions $(h_n)_n\subset C(\beta X)$, there exists $\nu\in M_p(X)$ such that $\mu(h_n)=\nu(h_n)$ for all $n$;
\item[{\rm (v)}]
\[
M(\beta f)(M_q(X))\subset M_p(Y),
\]
for any separable metric space $Y$ and continuous surjective mapping $f: X\to Y$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- cor-1: body_md -->
\label{c:main:1}
If $X$ is pseudocompact, then $X$ is universally $M_a^\ast$-measurable.
<!-- end cor-1 -->
<!-- cor-2: body_md -->
\label{c:main:2}
Any space is universally $M_{[\tau,\sigma]}$-measurable.
<!-- end cor-2 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{p:pmpu:1}
Let $X$ be a space, $p,q\in\{a,\sigma,\tau,R,\beta,d\}$, and $Q\in \{M,M^+,U,U^+,P\}$.
If $X$ is a universally $Q_{[p,q]}$-measurable space, then $X$ is a universally $Q_{[p,q]}^\ast$-measurable space.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{t:pmpu:2}
Let $X$ be a space, $p,q\in\{a,\sigma,\tau,R,\beta,d\}$, and $Q\in \{M^+,U,P\}$.
If $X$ is a universally $Q_{[p,q]}^\ast$-measurable space, then $X$ is a universally $M_{[p,q]}$-measurable space.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{t:pmpu:3}
Let $X$ be a space and $p,q\in\{a,\sigma,\tau,R,\beta,d\}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[{\rm (i)}]
A space $X$ is a universally $P_{[p,q]}$-measurable space
if and only if $X$ is a universally $M^+_{[p,q]}$-measurable space.
\item[{\rm (ii)}]
A space $X$ is a universally $P^\ast_{[p,q]}$-measurable space
if and only if $X$ is a universally $M^{+^\ast}_{[p,q]}$-measurable space.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- problem-2: body_md -->
Let $p,q\in\{f,\sigma,\tau,R,\beta,d\}$.
How are the following classes of spaces related?
\begin{itemize}
\item
universally $P_{[p,q]}$-measurable spaces;
\item
universally $P^\ast_{[p,q]}$-measurable spaces;
\item
universally $U_{[p,q]}$-measurable spaces;
\item
universally $U^\ast_{[p,q]}$-measurable spaces;
\item
universally $M_{[p,q]}$-measurable spaces.
\end{itemize}
<!-- end problem-2 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{p:defs:2}
Let $Y$ be a compact space and $X\subset Y$.
Then $w(X)=w(P(X))=w(P_\tau(X))$ and
\begin{align*}
P(X) &= \bbset\mu \in P(Y): \mu_*(X)=1\eeset,
&
P_\tau(X) &= \bbset\mu \in P(Y): \mu^*(X)=1\eeset.
\end{align*}
The embedding of $P(X)$ and $P_\tau(X)$ into $P(Y)$ is a topological embedding.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{l:lvs:rg}
Let $L_w$ be a locally convex linear space $L$ with the weak topology.
The space embeds, naturally and by an isomorphic homeomorphism, into $\mathbb R^\Gamma$ as a dense linear subspace, where $\Gamma$ is a Hamel basis of the dual space $L'$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
For $v\in L_w$ and $g\in \Gamma$, put $\varphi(v)(g)=g(v)$. The map $\varphi\colon L_w\to \mathbb R^\Gamma$ is the desired embedding.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{p:lvs:kappa}
Let $L_w$ be a locally convex linear space $L$ with the weak topology.
Then $L_w$ is perfectly $\kappa$-normal.
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
By Lemma \ref{l:lvs:rg}, we may assume that $L_w$ is a dense linear subspace of $\mathbb R^\Gamma$, where $\Gamma$ is a Hamel basis of the dual space $L'$.
The space $\mathbb R^\Gamma$ is perfectly $\kappa$-normal \cite{Shchepin1976}. Since $L_w$ is dense in $\mathbb R^\Gamma$, $L_w$ is perfectly $\kappa$-normal.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{t:lcs:c-emb}
Let $L_w$ be a locally convex linear space $L$ with the weak topology.
Then, for a dense subset $M\subset L_w$, the following conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item
$M$ is $C^*$-embedded in $L_w$;
\item
$M$ is $C$-embedded in $L_w$;
\item
$M$ is $G_\delta$-dense in $L_w$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
By Proposition \ref{p:lvs:kappa}, $L_w$ is perfectly $\kappa$-normal.
The theorem now follows from Lemma 9.9.35, Theorem 6.1.5, Proposition 6.1.6, Theorem 6.1.7, Lemma 8.4.5, and Theorem 9.9.36 of \cite{at2009}.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{t:lcs:}
Let $L_w$ be a locally convex linear space $L$ with the weak topology and let $M\subset L_w$ be a dense subset.
For every continuous function $f\colon M\to \mathbb R$ there exists a sequence $(g_n)_{n\in\omega}\subset L'$ of continuous functionals such that $f=h\circ g$, where
\[
g\colon M\to \mathbb R^\omega,\ g(v)(n)=g_n(v)
\]
and $h\colon g(M)\to \mathbb R$ is some continuous function.
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
By Lemma \ref{l:lvs:rg}, we may assume that $L_w$ is a dense linear subspace of $\mathbb R^\Gamma$, where $\Gamma$ is a Hamel basis of the dual space $L'$.
Then $M$ is dense in $\mathbb R^\Gamma$. By the factorization lemma 0.2.3 of \cite{Arhangelskii1989CpBook}, there exists an at most countable set $G\subset \Gamma$ such that $f=p \circ \pi_G$, where
\[
\pi_G\colon \mathbb R^\Gamma\to \mathbb R^G,\ \pi_G(s)(v)=s(v)
\]
is the projection and $p\colon \pi_G(M)\to \mathbb R$ is some continuous function. Enumerate the set $G$ as $G=\{g_n:n\in\omega\}$. The sequence $(g_n)_{n\in\omega}$ is the one required.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- cor-3: body_md -->
\label{c:lcs:}
Let $L_w$ be a locally convex linear space $L$ with the weak topology.
For every continuous function $f\colon L_w\to \mathbb R$ there exists a sequence $(g_n)_{n\in\omega}\subset L'$ of continuous functionals such that $f=h\circ g$, where
\[
g\colon L_w\to \mathbb R^\omega,\ g(v)(n)=g_n(v)
\]
and $h\colon g(L_w)\to \mathbb R$ is some continuous function.
<!-- end cor-3 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
We assume that $p\neq q$.

Theorem \ref{t:lcs:c-emb} implies the equivalence of items (i), (ii), and (iii) of Theorem \ref{t:main:1}.

(iv)$\Leftrightarrow$(v) is easily verified.

(iii)$\Leftrightarrow$(v)
We show that $M_q(Y)$ has a countable pseudocharacter.
If $q=a$, then $M_p(X)\subset M_\sigma(X)$, and $M_\sigma(X)$ is $G_\delta$-dense in $M(\beta X)$. Consequently, $X$ is pseudocompact. Then $Y$ is a metrizable compactum and $M_q(Y)=M(Y)$ has a countable network. If $q\neq a$, then $M_q(Y)\subset M_\tau(Y)$ has a countable network.

Since $M_p(X)$ is $G_\delta$-dense in $M_q(X)$, it follows that $M(\beta f)(M_p(X))$ is $G_\delta$-dense in $M(\beta f)(M_q(X))\subset M_q(Y)$. Consequently, $M(\beta f)(M_p(X))=M(\beta f)(M_q(X))\subset M_q(Y)$.

(iv)$\Leftrightarrow$(iii) Assume the contrary, that $M_p(X)$ is not $G_\delta$-dense in $M_{q}(X)$.
Let $G\subset M_{q}(X)\setminus M_p(X)$ be a nonempty null set and $\mu\in G$. Then there exists a sequence of functions $(h_n)_n\subset C(\beta X)$ such that $F=\bigcap_n h^{-1}_n(h_n(\mu))\subset G$.
Since $F\subset M_{q}(X)\setminus M_p(X)$, condition (iv) is violated.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
